newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves $30 mln Togo loan for fiscal program.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves $30 mln Togo loan for fiscal program.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday approved a $30 million loan for Togo to support the government's 1997 economic program.
The IMF said the third annual loan, issued under its Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility, would be repayable over 10 years.

The IMF said the government's fiscal program for 1997 aims to reduce the overall deficit to 4.3 percent of gross domestic product from 6.5 percent in 1996. To attain the target, tax system and administration reforms will continue with IMF support.
The government also plans to restructure its domestic debt, funded in part with resources from the privatization program, the IMF said in a statement.

"The resumption of fiscal consolidation and successful implementation of the various structural reforms in 1997 will be the determining factors of the government's commitment to accelerating the reform process and creating the conditions for sustained growth," the IMF said.
The IMF said Togo's performance in 1996 under the economic program was "mixed."
